issues.legal_issue: A statutory first charge for tax dues on a dealer’s property extends to the whole property and takes priority over a mortgage created before the charge arose.
material_facts: A bank advanced money under a cash credit facility secured by a mortgage over the debtor’s factory property.
The mortgage was created before a statutory provision made tax dues a first charge on the dealer’s property.
The tax authority claimed unpaid sales tax from the proceeds of a court-ordered sale of the mortgaged property, and the lower courts gave the tax claim priority over the bank’s mortgage claim.
The bank appealed the decision on priority.
issues.conclusion: The statutory first charge applies to the entire property, including the mortgagee’s interest, and has priority over the earlier mortgage; the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 11-AAAA of the Rajasthan Sales Tax Act, 1954, creates a first charge on the dealer’s property for tax and other sums due under the Act. Under Sections 58 and 100 of the Transfer of Property Act, a mortgage transfers an interest in property, while a charge secures payment without such a transfer. Dattatreya Shanker Mote v. Anand Chintaman Datar (1974) explains that a charge is wider than a mortgage and includes a mortgage. The Court also relied on Westminster City Council v. Haymarket Publishing Ltd. (1981), which held that a statutory charge on land could take priority over a pre-existing mortgage and extend to all existing estates and interests in the property.

rule.if: tax_debt_on_dealer_property and statute_creates_first_charge and prior_mortgage and appeal_over_sale_proceeds_priority

predicates.tax_debt_on_dealer_property: A dealer incurred tax or other statutory dues payable in respect of the dealer’s property.
predicates.statute_creates_first_charge: A statute made the relevant dues a first charge on the dealer’s property.
predicates.prior_mortgage: The dealer had mortgaged the property before the statutory first charge arose.
predicates.appeal_over_sale_proceeds_priority: A party appealed a decision determining whether the statutory dues or the mortgage claim had priority in sale proceeds.

issues.definition: When statutory dues on a dealer’s property are made a first charge, a prior mortgage exists, and an appeal concerns priority in sale proceeds, the first charge covers the whole property and prevails over the mortgage.
